props.label: What is pipe relining?
props.html:
What it is

What is pipe relining?

Pipe relining is a trenchless way to repair a damaged pipe from the inside. Instead of digging up and replacing the old pipe, we insert a resin-saturated liner into it, shape it against the pipe wall and cure it in place. Once it hardens you have a new pipe formed inside the old one.

It is ideal for pipes that are cracked, leaking or invaded by tree roots but still hold their basic shape. Because there is no excavation, it protects paving, gardens, driveways and concrete, which is why so many Sydney homeowners and strata managers choose it over a full dig and replace.

props.label: How pipe relining works
props.html:
How it works

How pipe relining works

A clear process, camera-checked at both ends.

1

Camera inspection

We run a CCTV camera through the pipe to confirm relining is right and measure the damage.

2

Clean the pipe

High-pressure water jetting clears roots, grease and debris so the liner bonds properly.

3

Install the liner

A resin-saturated liner is fed into the pipe and inflated against the wall.

4

Cure in place

The liner cures into a hard, seamless new pipe within the old one.

5

Final camera check

We camera the finished reline so you can see the repair and the flow.

props.html:

Relining or replacement, which do you need?

Relining suits most damaged pipes. Replacement is for pipes that have collapsed or lost their shape.

Pipe reliningPipe replacement
Digging requiredNone in most casesExcavation needed
Best forCracks, leaks, root damageCollapsed or badly deformed pipes
Disruption to siteMinimalHigher, site reinstated after
Typical timeframeOften a single dayLonger, depends on access

props.label: When pipe relining is the right fix
props.html:
When it suits

When pipe relining is the right fix

Relining works well when the pipe is damaged but not collapsed. It is a strong option if you have:

  • Cracked or fractured drain and sewer pipes
  • Tree roots getting in through joints
  • Leaks that keep causing blockages
  • Pipes under paving, driveways or established gardens
  • A heritage or hard-to-access property where digging is difficult

props.label: Pipe relining questions
props.html:
Good to know

Pipe relining questions

A properly installed reline is built to be a long-term repair and is designed to outlast the original pipe. We camera the finished job so you can see the result before we leave.

Cost depends on the length, diameter and condition of the pipe and how easy it is to access. We inspect first with a camera and give you an upfront price before any work starts, with no call-out fee.

In most cases, no. Relining is done through existing access points, so paving, driveways and gardens usually stay untouched. If a pipe has collapsed we will talk you through replacement instead.

Most cracked, leaking or root-damaged pipes can be relined. A pipe that has fully collapsed or lost its shape may need replacement, which we also do. The CCTV inspection tells us which is right.
